headline: Benazir Ahmed granted bail in UAE court, Bangladesh seeks cancellation
summary: Former IGP Benazir Ahmed, arrested on an Interpol Red Notice, has been granted bail by a UAE court. Bangladesh's government is now working to cancel the bail and secure his return for trial.
details: Former Inspector General of Police Benazir Ahmed has been granted bail by a court in the United Arab Emirates. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed confirmed this, stating the bail condition requires Benazir to remain in the UAE.

The minister noted that he is awaiting the full terms of the bail order. The Bangladesh government has already appointed a law firm in the UAE to pursue the cancellation of Benazir's bail and facilitate his return.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam confirmed ongoing communication between Bangladesh and UAE governments regarding the matter. She expressed hope that Benazir can be brought back to Bangladesh soon to face trial.

Benazir Ahmed, once a powerful law enforcement official, was arrested by Dubai Police on June 12 following an Interpol Red Notice requested by Bangladesh. The Directorate General of Federal Criminal Police in Abu Dhabi informed Bangladesh of the arrest.

The Interpol Red Notice, updated in April 2025, details allegations of Benazir concealing assets worth Tk 2.62 crore and acquiring Tk 9.44 crore beyond his known income sources. The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) accused him of abusing his office to accumulate illicit wealth.

A Metropolitan Senior Special Judge’s Court in Dhaka issued an arrest warrant against him on February 12, 2025. The Red Notice sought his location and provisional arrest pending extradition, listing several countries he might visit.

The ACC submitted a charge sheet against Benazir last November over illicit wealth accumulation, concealment, and money laundering, with the case now under trial. He faces five other corruption cases and trials before the International Crimes Tribunal for alleged crimes against humanity.

These include cases linked to enforced disappearances and torture during his tenure as RAB chief, and the 2013 crackdown on Hefazat-e-Islam supporters. International rights groups and the US have previously raised concerns over human rights violations under his leadership, with the US imposing sanctions in 2021.

headline_marked: [[Power cuts intensify across Bangladesh]] due to gas shortage, impacting daily life and industry
headline: Power cuts intensify across Bangladesh due to gas shortage, impacting daily life and industry
summary: Prolonged outages are affecting households, businesses, and industries nationwide, stemming from a significant drop in pipeline gas supply following an LNG terminal accident.
details: Power cuts have intensified across Bangladesh, with large parts of the country facing prolonged outages even after midnight. This widespread electricity shortage is disrupting households, businesses, and industrial production.
The situation deteriorated after the country’s pipeline gas supply dropped by over 17 percent. This followed a July 22 accident at an Excelerate Energy-operated liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal.

The average daily power generation shortfall reached 1,482 megawatts (MW) last week, a significant increase from 320MW the previous week. Hourly data showed the shortfall touching around 3,000MW in the early hours of Sunday.

This prolonged deficit forces distribution companies to rotate load-shedding for hours across different areas. Consumers are left without electricity at regular intervals throughout the day and night, with rural areas most severely impacted.

For households, these cuts disrupt cooking, study, and daily activities. Businesses are losing operating hours, while factories struggle to maintain production schedules due to unreliable power on top of inadequate gas supplies.

Jashim Uddin, a rice mill operator in Mymensingh, reported not getting electricity for at least seven hours yesterday, leading to idle employees. Farmers and irrigation-dependent businesses, like fish farmer Rahmat Ullah in Cumilla, also face severe challenges.

PGCB data indicates load-shedding in all eight divisions, with Dhaka division experiencing the highest shortages. This includes industrial hubs such as Savar, Narayanganj, and Gazipur, along with Mymensingh, Khulna, Rajshahi, and Rangpur.

The Bangladesh Power Development Board (PDB) is now forced to use increasingly expensive generation methods to limit the shortage. Gas supply to power plants has fallen significantly, leading to reliance on furnace-oil and even diesel-fired plants during peak hours.
